analysis: Changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md adds a load-time shape-warmup description (changed head range 956-991; the units supplied show only unrelated unchanged surrounding text at lines 1644-2284), and docs/provider/cli-reference.md line 1751 adds a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env var row. No code, wire protocol, attestation, key, or authorization behavior changes. Relevant threats considered: T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT oracle) and T-010/T-029 (availability). The documented warmup runs a solo prompt plus a served-width cell using artifact default sampling, is excluded from rate and counter training, has a 20 s wall budget, and a retry on preemption. No consumer data is involved. Synthetic prompts shouldn't touch the SSD prefix cache or its cacheSalt scoping. If warmup donations were written to the SSD tier, or the warmup prompts shared a scope with consumer traffic, that could affect T-041 timing signals. That is not shown in the supplied evidence; the implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration) is not in the batch. The env var is operator-local (daemon env), and disabling or skipping the probe only affects performance, so it adds no remote attack surface. The 'always' mode skips the shader-cache probe, a minor availability-only effect. Remaining integration question: confirm in the code PR that warmup requests bypass prefix-cache donation/adoption and calibration requests cannot be triggered by a consumer. The hunk at lines 956-991 was only partially visible and truncated, so this deserves a quick follow-up but is not a finding.
